overview:
Southwest Georgia's 2nd District leans Democratic by about four points, and Sanford Bishop has held the seat for decades. He enters the general election with a large financial edge, having raised over $1.1 million and reporting roughly $448,000 on hand, while Republican Matt Day has raised about $206,000 and reports under $2,000 available. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, and prediction markets put Bishop's chances near 93%.

With no polling to consult, the outlook rests on district lean, incumbency, and money, all of which favor Bishop. The expected margin sits around seventeen to eighteen points, though uncertainty runs wider than in well-polled contests. The seat remains in the Safe Democratic column, with the main risk being a late shift in the national environment or unexpected outside spending on either side.
